memory.content: render_invoice is read-only: it must never call issue_number() or otherwise touch NEXT_INVOICE. A draft (number == 0) renders with the header "INVOICE DRAFT"; only an issued invoice renders "INVOICE #<n>". Rendering the same Invoice twice must produce byte-identical output. Regression test: billing::tests::draft_preview_is_stable_and_does_not_consume_numbers.

Bug (fixed after af8cc59): render_invoice used to call issue_number() whenever invoice.number == 0, so every preview of an unsent draft consumed a fresh sequence number. Symptoms: the draft preview showed a different number each time, and those numbers were absent from the ledger (gaps). Also silently triggered by session_index_capacity_hint / vault_queue_capacity_hint / vault_cache_capacity_hint, which render an empty draft just to measure its length. Fix: render "INVOICE DRAFT" for number 0 and never allocate in the renderer.

Invoice::issue (via issue_number) is the ONLY place allowed to advance the global NEXT_INVOICE sequence. The ledger must be gap-free, so a number may only be consumed at the moment an invoice is actually issued — never during preview, rendering, length measurement, or any other read path. number == 0 is the sentinel for "draft / not yet issued"; do not assign real numbers anywhere else.

issue_number() has a side effect: each call permanently consumes one number from the global NEXT_INVOICE sequence (fetch_add), and there is no way to give it back. Never call it from a "look but don't touch" path (rendering, previewing, sizing, logging) — doing so creates ledger gaps. If you only need to display something for a draft, use the "INVOICE DRAFT" placeholder instead. Tests share this global across threads, so assertions on exact sequence values are racy; compare outputs instead.
